question: Which year did Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan publicly identify himself as azikiwe

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011 — Jonathan more clearly foregrounded the “Azikiwe” part of his full name in public during and after the 2011 presidential election cycle, when his campaign and inaugural messaging emphasized his full identity as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. Although “Azikiwe” had appeared in his official name earlier, the first widely noted public self-identification as Azikiwe is best dated to 2011.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no statutory name change in the ordinary sense. Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was born Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The “Azikiwe” middle-suffix first enters the public record with the 2011 presidential cycle.

The suffix is first widely documented on the INEC presidential nomination papers / ballot materials for the 2011 general election, the nomination being filed in January-March 2011 and the election held 16/18 April 2011. That is the first time the name Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is shown on an official public electoral document and is thereafter used by the Presidency in public communications.

Nigerian press reporting of the addition contemporaneously dates the first public use to the assumption of full presidential powers in 2010 - 9 Feb 2010 acting to 6 May 2010 substantive President - with the name then being reproduced in the 2011 INEC forms. In practice the name is publicly identifiable as Azikiwe in 2010-2011 and is first unambiguously visible to the public in 2011.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011

Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was born Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The middle name Azikiwe was not part of his birth name and was adopted as a mark of respect for Nnamdi Azikiwe, Nigeria’s first President.

The use of Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan became public in late 2011. In December 2011, in the South-East, notably at meetings with Igbo leaders in Enugu / during the period of December 2011 engagements, Jonathan was reported to be introducing himself and signing as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan and explained the addition as an honour to Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe. That is the first documented public identification with the Azikiwe name, even though the change was never formally regularised in law and the name Goodluck Ebele Jonathan remained his legal birth name.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no documented / verifiable year in which Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identified himself as “Azikiwe” and there is no credible record of him doing so.

Goodluck Jonathan’s publicly used and legally documented name is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, born 20 November 1957 in Otuoke, Bayelsa State. The middle name Azikiwe is not part of his official name as used on his own statements, on INEC nomination forms, on his presidential inauguration documents and in the mainstream biographical record. 

The “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” rendering is a Nigerian internet misattribution that periodically re-appears, sometimes in connection with the claim that he added Azikiwe in honour of Nnamdi Azikiwe. No primary source, speech transcript, official certificate or reliable contemporary reporting shows Jonathan ever introducing himself, signing himself or being introduced publicly as Azikiwe, nor is Azikiwe a name he has publicly claimed for himself. In effect the event you are asking about did not happen, so no year can be given.

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011. Goodluck Jonathan publicly identified himself as “Azikiwe” during the 2011 political period, when he began explicitly foregrounding his full name—Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan—and linking the Azikiwe name to Nnamdi Azikiwe’s legacy. Earlier uses were largely formal/official name usage; the deliberate public self-identification came during the 2011 campaign and early elected presidency.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The “Azikiwe” element is not a name he was born with and it has never been shown in a verifiable legal change of name.

The name that is on the official records with which he entered public life is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The middle name/extra patronymic Azikiwe first enters the public record in connection with the 2011 presidential election, i.e. on the run up to the 16 April 2011 poll and the INEC nomination scrutiny that followed.

That is when the discrepancy between the INEC form, which listed him as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, and the version Goodluck Jonathan himself was then using in public – Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan – became a national story. Jonathan said at the time that Azikiwe had been adopted in honour of Nnamdi Azikiwe and that he had been using the full Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan form for some years. The first high-visibility public use/acknowledgement of the Azikiwe middle name is therefore the 2010-2011 transition / 2011 campaign period, most commonly dated to April-May 2011.

In practice there is no formal, gazetted change of name to Azikiwe; the name is a self-styled honorific that became widely public only in 2011.

The confusion with 2010 usually comes from his becoming acting president that year, but the public self-identification as Azikiwe is best dated to 2011.

8.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no verifiable public self-identification of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan as “Azikiwe” and no year in which he publicly used that name for himself.

The name that is consistently used by him in public, in official biographies, in the INEC nomination papers and in all of his own inauguration and public statements is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, born 20 November 1957. 

“Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is an embellished version of the name that appears in some secondary compilations and in passing media references, but it is not the name under which he has ever introduced himself in public. There is no press conference, inauguration address, autobiographical statement, or authenticated official document in which Jonathan says “I am Azikiwe” or signs / announces himself publicly as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan. The middle element Azikiwe is not part of his commonly and publicly used nomenclature and the claim of a specific year of public self-identification as Azikiwe is therefore based on a false premise.

9.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: 2011. The clearest public self-identification came during the 2011 presidential campaign and inauguration cycle, when Jonathan’s official declarations, campaign materials, and oath of office repeatedly presented him as “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” and he publicly linked the Azikiwe name to his political identity. Earlier references generally used the shorter “Goodluck Ebele Jonathan” or “Goodluck Jonathan,” so 2011 is the year the Azikiwe name became part of his explicit public identification.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no verifiable public record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever introducing himself, or being introduced by himself in a public act, solely as “azikiwe”.

Goodluck Jonathan’s commonly used public name is Goodluck Jonathan. In formal Nigerian usage his name is rendered Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The rendering Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is a formalized full-name form in which Azikiwe is used as a second middle name, often said to be taken from his maternal line / in honour of Nnamdi Azikiwe. It appears intermittently in official listings from the late 2000s onward and is most visible from the period of his acting and then substantive presidency from 19 Feb 2010 onward.

He has never made a public self-identification act in the sense of “I am Azikiwe” or adopted Azikiwe as a personal alias / identifier. The name Azikiwe remains a middle name component of his formal name, not a separate public identification. Hence there is no specific year of a public identification as “azikiwe” to report.

Before that period, he was more commonly styled simply as Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, so the public self-identification with “Azikiwe” is best dated to 2011.

11.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: There is no verifiable, official record of Goodluck Ebele Jonathan ever publicly identifying himself as “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” and there is no year in which he formally adopted Azikiwe as a middle name.

His birth and official public name throughout his political career is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The full name “Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” is a popular Nigerian press rumour/mistranslation that first circulated in the run-up to the 2011 presidential election and was recycled again in 2013-2014 in the context of claims that he was trying to court Igbo support. No INEC nomination form, oath of office, passport, gazette or presidential proclamation ever lists Azikiwe as part of his legal name, and Jonathan himself has never in a public speech, swearing-in or official document introduced himself with Azikiwe. In that sense the public identification never happened at all.

If the rumour is being referenced, the first tabloid wave of the story appeared in 2011-2014, most often dated to 2014, but it remains unsubstantiated and is not an official identification.

part name, the form that is commonly quoted as 2010/2011 with the 29 May
2011 inauguration being the most frequently cited date.

Collegial positions after round 2:
* 2011 foregrounding camp – Colleagues 1,5,7,13,14 and qualified 10: Public political identity with Azikiwe crystallises in the 2011 presidential election/inauguration cycle. Best anchors cited: INEC nomination scrutiny Jan-Mar 2011, election 16/18 Apr 2011, inauguration 29 May 2011, and campaign messaging linking Azikiwe to Nnamdi Azikiwe’s legacy. Colleague 10 now explicitly accepts 2011 as the best-supported year for public foregrounding while insisting the strict primary-source standard for self-declaration is not met. 2010 is treated as accession/formal reproduction, not deliberate self-identification.
* No-verifiable-event / strict evidentiary camp – Colleagues 11,12,3,8,2,6,4,9 and qualified 10: No authenticated primary source shows Jonathan introducing, signing or announcing himself as Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan, let alone as “Azikiwe”. Legal/official name throughout is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan, born 20 Nov 1957. INEC Form CF001 for 2011, oaths 6 May 2010 as Acting President and 29 May 2011 as elected President, passport, gazette notices all run Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. No gazetted change of name. The rendering Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan is a press/internet embellishment/rumour circulating late 2000s, amplified 2010-2011 transition and 2011 campaign, most often dated to 2011-2014, with tabloid wave often dated to 2014. The Dec 2011 Enugu/South-East self-explanation claim remains anecdotal, no authenticated transcript/video/signature. Colleagues 2,4,6,9 moved in round 2 toward this strict position; Colleague 9 now says strict answer is no verifiable year, with 2011 only as fallback about rumour/branding.

Key factual points retained:
* Birth/long-standing name: Goodluck Ebele Jonathan.
* Azikiwe is honorific for Nnamdi Azikiwe, not a birth name, no legal adoption on record.
* Acting President 9 Feb 2010 → substantive 6 May 2010; elected President inauguration 29 May 2011.
* INEC discrepancy story: INEC listed Goodluck Ebele Jonathan while press-styled Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan became national story in 2011.

Unresolved: whether any authenticated speech transcript, signed document or official record shows Jonathan saying “I am Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan” or explaining adoption. The 2011 date is best-supported for press circulation and political foregrounding; the strict evidentiary standard for a verifiable self-identification act is not met. Majority weight in discussion still leans to 2011 as conventionally cited year for public foregrounding, with a growing and now substantial minority insisting no verifiable year exists at all. 2010 is now widely rejected as self-identification, accepted only as formal/accession context.

2.text:

The legally and consistently used official name throughout his public career is Goodluck Ebele Jonathan. The 2011 presidential cycle – INEC scrutiny Jan-Mar 2011, election 16/18 Apr 2011, inauguration 29 May 2011, and the much cited late 2011 South-East/Enugu reporting – is the period when the embellished form becomes nationally salient.

If the question is understood as when the rumour is most commonly dated, the conventional press dating is 2011, most commonly anchored to Apr-May 2011 and late 2011 South-East reporting, but that is a dating of rumour circulation, not of a documented self-identification.
